claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr exhibits anomalous stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior.
Differential thermal expansion among the principal elements generates internal stress fields.
The thermally induced internal stress fields are the primary cause of the anomalous stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior.
Thermally induced internal stresses promote localized short-range atomic ordering.
Localized short-range atomic ordering promotes dislocation pinning.
Internal stresses, short-range ordering, and dislocation pinning alter creep, hardness, strain hardening, and elastic responses over a wide temperature range.
The as-solidified or as-processed alloy contains compositional inhomogeneities.
The as-solidified or as-processed alloy contains residual internal stresses caused by thermal-expansion mismatch among its constituent elements.
High-temperature pre-annealing will homogenize the microstructure and relieve thermal-expansion-induced residual stresses.
Rapid cooling after pre-annealing will freeze in a reduced level of internal stress and short-range order.
Relaxing residual stresses by pre-annealing will diminish short-range atomic ordering.
A diminished level of short-range ordering will alter the alloy's mechanical and thermoelastic responses.
Relative to the as-processed alloy, the stress-relieved specimen will exhibit reduced anomalies in elastic moduli over 293–1100 K.
The stress-relieved specimen will exhibit thermoelastic behavior closer to the predicted thermal-expansion behavior.
Pre-annealing will decrease hardening after aging at 600–800 °C because fewer thermally activated ordering events will occur.
Pre-annealing will likely increase the creep rate at approximately 1250 °C by reducing dislocation pinning.
Thermal-expansion mismatch is significant from room temperature to approximately 1250 °C.
Diffusive atomic rearrangements relevant to the proposed mechanism occur notably during aging at 600–800 °C.
Outside the stated temperature ranges, other deformation and strengthening mechanisms might dominate.
